_about: Inductive schemes and laws tested in research/2026-11-14_opus_route-induction. Instance ids: V = vertices, gid = index in `plantri -b -a V` output order (plantri 4.5), t0 = face index in code/tri.py from_rotation order, x = degree-4 vertex, vertex labels 0-based (plantri letter a = 0), merge q->p. 'range' is the exhaustive range tested.

refuted.statement: Lift lemma, only-if half (route-graph-theory PROOFS Lemma 6.2(iii)): if the lift s of s' is a TM then s' is a TM
refuted.lesson: splitting v can open a cycle of tau'; s TM iff split(tau')+a v1 is a spanning tree of T-x (PROOFS Prop 2.1)

refuted.statement: Degree-4 contraction preserves the existence of a pair
refuted.range: V<=17, fails in 7,510 of 131,336 simple contractions
refuted.lesson: contraction can create a black-inner separating triangle; choose the contraction (conjecture G)

refuted.statement: Every TM of T/M lifts to a TM of T
refuted.range: V<=17, fails in 41,873 of 131,336 simple contractions
refuted.lesson: the lift condition a in K2 is global; failing TMs must be sent to N-type TMs (rotation rho)

refuted.statement: Failing lifts are compensated within the same type (B >= b)
refuted.lesson: compensation comes from the other contraction's type (C >= b holds)

refuted.statement: Some TM of T/M satisfies the local condition LC (edge a v in Q)
refuted.range: V<=17, fails in 6,474 of 131,336 simple contractions
refuted.lesson: a one-edge local prescription is too strong as an induction hypothesis

refuted.statement: rho(lift) is a TM for every failing lift
refuted.lesson: rotation covers 98.7%; the case b in K2' needs a second rule
contraction inequality is tight: TM(T) = TM(T/M) occurs often

refuted.statement: lowest coefficient lc = sum over D with c_min cycles of prod_C (white faces inside C) is monotone under contraction
refuted.lesson: c_min can drop under expansion (1 vs 3), resetting lc; signed-polynomial data is not monotone

refuted.range: V<=17; c_min(T) <= c_min(T/M) always holds, equality fails in 358 simple contractions

refuted.statement: Skein relation TM(T) = TM(T/M) + TM(T/N) (both merges defined)
refuted.range: V<=17: fails in 24,600 of 172,436 vertex-root pairs, in both directions; least squares over V<=16 leaves max residual 14.5
refuted.lesson: only #states satisfies the deletion-contraction identity (PROOFS Prop 1.1); TM and pairs do not, because pairs mix M- and N-types

refuted.statement: Prescribed corner: for every face t in A and non-root corner u, some TM has s(t)=u (HCs); same for the mate r (HCr)
refuted.range: V<=15: HCs holds in only 13 of 1,794 rooted instances with a pair (8 of them octahedron roots)
refuted.lesson: local prescriptions at a face are generally impossible; consistent with NP-completeness of prescribing edge sets

refuted.statement: A good contraction (result has a pair) always exists
refuted.range: V<=15; no failure without separating triangles
refuted.lesson: separating triangles must be handled by gluing (multiplicativity), not contraction

smallest.note: octahedron: every P-reduction is non-simple and loses the pair

refuted.range: V<=15: 1,865 of 7,173 P-reductions (rooted, avoiding t0) lose the pair
refuted.lesson: P-reduction is less useful than Q-reduction; TM(T) >= TM(T'') still holds

surviving.statement: Contraction inequality TM(T) >= TM(T/M) for every degree-4 contraction avoiding t0 (multigraph results allowed)
Some TM of T/M lifts to a TM of T (when T/M has a TM)
C >= b: N-type TMs of T are at least as many as non-lifting TMs of T/M
Good contraction exists for rooted instances with a pair and no separating triangle, V>6
surviving.range: 8<=V<=15 (1,154 rooted instances); the octahedron is the base case

surviving.statement: states, pairs, D monotone under contraction; c_min(T) <= c_min(T/M)
No frozen face: for each face t in A and each corner u some TM has s(t) != u
Octahedron insertion into a white face doubles TM; into a black face kills all pairs
